issues.title: EQ engine not affecting sound; band shapes don't save
issues.body:
What happened


Can't get the audio engine to affect the sound. I had to reapply it to the output a bunch of times to get the EQ engine to run. Now the warnings are gone but it doesn't change the sound I turn all the bands down.


The band shapes don't save. When I click one of the filter shapes, the callout closes and doesn't save what I chose.


Also, the band shapes seem weird. Usually in EQ apps, bands are hump shaped, but here they look more like a cusp going the opposite way. What I really want is the usual hump shape with a Q-factor so I can fix bass peaks and dips surgically.
Cool app otherwise.
Setup









FluidEQ
1.7.4


Windows
Windows_NT 10.0.26200 x64


Electron
43.2.0


Audio engine
FluidEQ Engine


Equalizer APO
NOT installed


FluidEQ Engine
installed

issues.bodyHtml:
What happened

  1. Can't get the audio engine to affect the sound. I had to reapply it to the output a bunch of times to get the EQ engine to run. Now the warnings are gone but it doesn't change the sound I turn all the bands down.

  2. The band shapes don't save. When I click one of the filter shapes, the callout closes and doesn't save what I chose.

Also, the band shapes seem weird. Usually in EQ apps, bands are hump shaped, but here they look more like a cusp going the opposite way. What I really want is the usual hump shape with a Q-factor so I can fix bass peaks and dips surgically.

Cool app otherwise.

Setup
FluidEQ 1.7.4
Windows Windows_NT 10.0.26200 x64
Electron 43.2.0
Audio engine FluidEQ Engine
Equalizer APO NOT installed
FluidEQ Engine installed

comments.body:
Thanks for the report, and for including the logs — they showed exactly what went wrong.
1. The EQ doesn't change the sound. Your logs show the engine running on your Samsung output but never on the HAYLOU S30. Some Bluetooth headsets only pick up effects from a place in Windows that 1.7.4 never tries, so every repair put the engine somewhere your headset doesn't read. FluidEQ 2.0 tries those places too. After updating:

If the app offers Update engine, accept it.
Play something on the headphones and allow the Windows permission prompts. It can take two or three before the engine lands where your headset reads it.

2. Filter shapes not saving. That was a bug: picking a shape counted as a click outside the band, so the panel closed before your choice was saved. Fixed in 2.0.
3. The band shape. Your bands already are the usual bell (Peak). They just start fairly narrow (Q 2), and on a graph spanning 10 Hz to 20 kHz that looks pointy. Use the Quality (Q) dial next to Filter in the Selected band panel: turn it down for a wide hump, up for narrow cuts on bass peaks and dips. You can also hold Ctrl and scroll over a selected band's point on the graph.
FluidEQ 2.0 comes out soon. Please try it, and if your headset still doesn't change, send a new report from inside 2.0 so we can see what the new version tried.
Thanks, and glad you like the app!
comments.bodyHtml:
Thanks for the report, and for including the logs — they showed exactly what went wrong.

1. The EQ doesn't change the sound. Your logs show the engine running on your Samsung output but never on the HAYLOU S30. Some Bluetooth headsets only pick up effects from a place in Windows that 1.7.4 never tries, so every repair put the engine somewhere your headset doesn't read. FluidEQ 2.0 tries those places too. After updating:

  • If the app offers Update engine, accept it.
  • Play something on the headphones and allow the Windows permission prompts. It can take two or three before the engine lands where your headset reads it.

2. Filter shapes not saving. That was a bug: picking a shape counted as a click outside the band, so the panel closed before your choice was saved. Fixed in 2.0.

3. The band shape. Your bands already are the usual bell (Peak). They just start fairly narrow (Q 2), and on a graph spanning 10 Hz to 20 kHz that looks pointy. Use the Quality (Q) dial next to Filter in the Selected band panel: turn it down for a wide hump, up for narrow cuts on bass peaks and dips. You can also hold Ctrl and scroll over a selected band's point on the graph.

FluidEQ 2.0 comes out soon. Please try it, and if your headset still doesn't change, send a new report from inside 2.0 so we can see what the new version tried.

Thanks, and glad you like the app!

issues.title: Bug report - FluidEQ Engine DSP Exciter causes intermittent audio cutouts
issues.body:
What happened
FluidEQ Engine DSP Exciter causes intermittent audio cutouts
Audio cutouts switches rapidly between sound and silence with a clipping sound
Issue appears to be related to overall amount of exciter processing rather than one specific band

Disabling DSP resumes normal playback, disabling exciter resumes normal playback, disabling or enabling other dsp functions seems to have no effect
Currently only using exciter, bass forge, bass punch
Enabling 2-3 exciter bands causes audio to cut out intermittently very rapidly
With bands enabled but amount set to 0, issue does not appear
Increasing amount causes issue to appear, not tied to any specific amount or band
Low mid high and organic bands can all contribute to issue, timing doesn't seem to affect issue
Activating an additional exciter band can also cause issue
Issue can occur even when individual band settings aren't high, maybe a cumulative processing threshold?
Bass forge does not cause audio cutouts, seems to be the harmonic generation in only the exciter
Unsure if issue was present before updating to 2.0.0

Setup









FluidEQ
2.0.0


Windows
Windows_NT 10.0.26200 x64


Electron
43.2.0


Audio engine
FluidEQ Engine


Equalizer APO
installed


FluidEQ Engine
installed

issues.bodyHtml:
What happened

FluidEQ Engine DSP Exciter causes intermittent audio cutouts
Audio cutouts switches rapidly between sound and silence with a clipping sound
Issue appears to be related to overall amount of exciter processing rather than one specific band

  • Disabling DSP resumes normal playback, disabling exciter resumes normal playback, disabling or enabling other dsp functions seems to have no effect
  • Currently only using exciter, bass forge, bass punch
  • Enabling 2-3 exciter bands causes audio to cut out intermittently very rapidly
  • With bands enabled but amount set to 0, issue does not appear
  • Increasing amount causes issue to appear, not tied to any specific amount or band
  • Low mid high and organic bands can all contribute to issue, timing doesn't seem to affect issue
  • Activating an additional exciter band can also cause issue
  • Issue can occur even when individual band settings aren't high, maybe a cumulative processing threshold?
  • Bass forge does not cause audio cutouts, seems to be the harmonic generation in only the exciter
  • Unsure if issue was present before updating to 2.0.0

Setup
FluidEQ 2.0.0
Windows Windows_NT 10.0.26200 x64
Electron 43.2.0
Audio engine FluidEQ Engine
Equalizer APO installed
FluidEQ Engine installed
